transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, my regular doctor actually sent me. She says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I can see it a bit—my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me lately when I'm on my shifts. But... to be honest with you, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and see that the number is lower. So, I guess that's why she wanted me to come in.
Can you tell me how you feel about gaining weight or if you've been doing anything to try to keep your weight low?

Well, the thought of gaining weight really does scare me. If I end up eating something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me right away. I end up checking myself in the mirror a lot, and I just can't stop thinking that I need to make up for it somehow.
Have you been doing anything, like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual, after you eat to try to prevent weight gain?

No, I don't do any of those things. I've never made myself sick, and I don't use laxatives or anything like that. 

As for exercise... well, I'm a building cleaner, so I'm already on my feet walking the floors and working all shift. That tires me out enough. I don't do any extra workouts or running around to try and burn off food. I mostly just try to avoid eating the things that worry me in the first place.
Can you tell me how you perceive your body weight or shape? Do you think you're underweight, normal weight, or overweight?

Well, it's a bit complicated. I know my doctor says I'm underweight, and like I said, my clothes are loose. But when I look at myself... I don't know, it's more about how I feel in my body. 

When I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. Like I'm in control. But if my stomach looks the least bit full in the mirror, or if I feel heavy, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So, I don't really see myself as too thin. I just see whether I'm keeping things tight and controlled, or if I'm failing at it.
Can you tell me how much weight you've lost recently, and whether you've ever felt that you've dropped below a healthy weight for your height?

I don't know the exact number of pounds I've lost recently, to be honest. But... well, my regular doctor says I've gotten too thin. And I do notice it with my clothes. My work pants are just hanging loose on me now when I'm doing my shifts. 

But as for feeling like I'm below a healthy weight... it's tough to explain. Even with the doctor telling me I weigh too little, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and see that the number is lower. I know what the charts say, but I just don't feel like it's a bad thing when the weight goes down.

Can you tell me what goes through your mind when you think about gaining even a small amount of weight—like, say, 5 pounds? Is it more about how it would change how you look, how you feel about yourself, or something else entirely?

Just the thought of gaining five pounds... it really scares me. I guess it's a mix of both how I look and how I feel about myself. 

If I happen to eat something heavier, like a few biscuits or some pasta, I'll spend the entire rest of the day just... scared that it's going to show on me right away. I end up checking myself in the mirror over and over, looking at my stomach. I just can't stop thinking that I need to make up for it somehow, so that the weight doesn't stick to me. It's just a constant worry.

When you worry about gaining weight, is it mainly about how it would affect your appearance, or is it more about what you believe it would mean about your health, your self-discipline, or something else?

I think it's mostly about the discipline, honestly. Like I mentioned before, when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. It means I'm in control of myself. But if I eat something and my stomach looks the least bit full in the mirror... I just feel like I've completely let myself go. It's not really about my health, it's just that feeling of failing to keep things tight and controlled.
Even though you're already underweight, does the idea of gaining even a small amount of weight still feel unacceptable to you?

Yes, it really does. Like I was saying a couple of minutes ago... if I eat something heavier, you know, some pasta or a few biscuits, I spend the rest of the day just terrified that it's going to show on my body. Gaining anything at all is just... no, I can't accept it. I end up checking myself over and over, and my mind just races trying to figure out how I need to make up for it so the weight doesn't stay on me.

When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as larger or heavier than you actually are, or is your fear more about what weight gain would mean to you emotionally or mentally, even if you know you're already thin?

I think it's mostly the emotional part, like I was just saying a minute ago. I know I'm thin. But when I look in the mirror and see that I'm small and neat, it just... it tells me I'm handling everything right. If I look in that same mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full to me, it's not just about looking heavier. I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So it really is about what it means to me mentally.

When you look at pictures of yourself or see yourself in reflections, do you feel that you appear thinner than you actually are, or is your main concern more about how you feel regarding control and discipline, regardless of how you actually look?

Well, like I keep saying, it really just comes back to that feeling of control. I don't look at a picture or a reflection and think I'm thinner than I actually am. It's exactly what I mentioned before—seeing myself small and neat in the mirror is what tells me I'm handling everything right in my life. If I catch my reflection and my stomach looks even a tiny bit full to me, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So, yes, it's definitely about the discipline and what it means to me, rather than misjudging how I actually look.

When you worry about gaining weight or eating something heavier, does it feel like even a small change in your body would make you look significantly different than you do now, or do you feel that your body would look about the same, but it's more about how you judge yourself mentally for having eaten it?

It's really about how I judge myself, just like I've been saying. I know a few biscuits won't physically change my body overnight. But mentally... well, when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. If my stomach looks the least bit full in the mirror, even if it's just from eating a normal meal, I feel like I've completely let myself go. It's not that I think I suddenly look huge, it's just that the fullness means I've failed.

When you worry about eating something that might lead to weight gain, is it mainly about maintaining a sense of control and discipline, or do you also feel a strong sense of guilt, shame, or concern about your self-worth because of it?

I know I sound like a broken record today, but it really all ties together for me. The guilt and the self-worth... it's all based on that same thing I keep mentioning. Keeping myself small and neat is basically how I prove to myself that I'm handling everything right in my life. 

So if I eat something heavier and then look in the mirror and see my stomach looking even a little bit full, the shame hits hard. It's a terrible feeling. It just makes me feel like I've completely let myself go and failed. So yes, my self-worth is very much wrapped up in it.
Has there been a point where you actively wanted to become thinner, or was it more about maintaining that sense of control, regardless of how thin you actually became?

I don't think there was ever a specific time where I just wanted to get thinner for the sake of being thin. It wasn't about hitting a certain number on the scale or anything like that. 

It really has always been about maintaining that control. Just... keeping things tight and disciplined. Like I said, staying small and neat is how I know I'm managing my life. So, no, I wouldn't say I actively tried to keep getting thinner and thinner. I just had to keep up the routine so I didn't feel like everything was falling apart.

Do you feel that your overall sense of who you are or how you feel about yourself is strongly connected to your weight or shape, so that if either changed, you would feel like a different or worse version of yourself?

Yes, I'd say they are very connected. Like I mentioned before, when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. It's how I know I'm doing okay. If my weight or shape changed... well, if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. It makes me feel like a worse version of myself, like I'm failing. So, yes, my shape and how I feel about myself are definitely tied together.

When you feel anxious or scared about possibly gaining weight, is it mainly because you want to avoid becoming fat, or is it more because gaining weight would make you feel like you’ve lost control or are failing yourself?

I think it's really both, honestly. It's that feeling of failing, but I am also just... scared of it showing on my body. Like, if I eat something heavier, like biscuits or some pasta, I'll spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me right away. I end up keeping on checking myself, looking in the mirror to see if it did. And then I just start thinking about how I need to make up for it somehow, just so I don't lose that grip on things.

When you feel scared about possibly gaining weight, is the main reason because you are afraid of what it would look like if you became fat, or is it more because gaining weight would make you feel like you’ve lost control or are failing yourself?

Well, I think I just answered that, didn't I? Like I was just saying, it's really both of those things. I don't think I can separate them. 

I'm afraid of what it would look like, yes, but looking fat also means I've lost control and failed myself. I'm not sure how else to explain it, to be honest. I don't really have a different answer for you... they just go hand in hand for me.
When you feel bad about yourself after eating something heavier, is it mainly because of the change in your shape, or more about the number on the scale or the idea of gaining weight?

I guess I'm not really sure how to separate those, either. I mean, they all kind of blend together for me. 

If I eat something heavier, I feel bad because I worry it'll change my shape, and I worry it'll make the number on the scale go up. It's just... all of it. I haven't really noticed if one bothers me more than the other. They just all make me feel like I've messed up.
When you think about gaining weight, is your main concern about how it would change the way you look, or is it more about what it would mean for your sense of control or discipline?

I... I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, Doctor. It's just like I was saying a minute ago. I really can't separate them. 

Changing the way I look and losing my discipline... to me, they are the exact same thing. If my body changes, it means I didn't have discipline. I just don't have a way to pick one over the other for you. They're completely tied together.

target_item.manifestation: When I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right, but if my stomach looks the least bit full in the mirror I feel like I've let myself go.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks if the patient's overall sense of self or self-worth is strongly connected to their weight or shape, which corresponds to the symptom of Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance (undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation).

patient.answer: Yes, I'd say they are very connected. Like I mentioned before, when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. It's how I know I'm doing okay. If my weight or shape changed... well, if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. It makes me feel like a worse version of myself, like I'm failing. So, yes, my shape and how I feel about myself are definitely tied together.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences persistent anxiety or fear about weight gain primarily due to a desire to avoid being fat, or if the fear is more closely tied to the sense of self and control regardless of actual weight concerns.
doctor.question: When you feel anxious or scared about possibly gaining weight, is it mainly because you want to avoid becoming fat, or is it more because gaining weight would make you feel like you’ve lost control or are failing yourself?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I spend the rest of the day scared it's going to show on me, so I keep checking myself and thinking I need to make up for it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's anxiety and fear regarding gaining weight and the underlying reasons for it, which aligns with the 'Fear_of_Weight_Gain' symptom profile.

patient.answer: I think it's really both, honestly. It's that feeling of failing, but I am also just... scared of it showing on my body. Like, if I eat something heavier, like biscuits or some pasta, I'll spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me right away. I end up keeping on checking myself, looking in the mirror to see if it did. And then I just start thinking about how I need to make up for it somehow, just so I don't lose that grip on things.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's fear of weight gain is primarily driven by a desire to avoid being fat (body image concern) or by the emotional impact of feeling like they have lost control (self-evaluation based on weight).
doctor.question: When you feel scared about possibly gaining weight, is the main reason because you are afraid of what it would look like if you became fat, or is it more because gaining weight would make you feel like you’ve lost control or are failing yourself?

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeating the exact same question as the previous turn, which I just answered using S045 (Fear_of_Weight_Gain). There is no new symptom to map to.

patient.answer:
Well, I think I just answered that, didn't I? Like I was just saying, it's really both of those things. I don't think I can separate them. 

I'm afraid of what it would look like, yes, but looking fat also means I've lost control and failed myself. I'm not sure how else to explain it, to be honest. I don't really have a different answer for you... they just go hand in hand for me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's fear of weight gain and self-evaluation is primarily based on shape or weight.
doctor.question: When you feel bad about yourself after eating something heavier, is it mainly because of the change in your shape, or more about the number on the scale or the idea of gaining weight?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking to differentiate between whether the patient feels bad due to a change in shape or due to the number on the scale/idea of gaining weight after eating something heavier. This is an attempt to clarify the nuances of the patient's body image disturbance (S046) vs fear of weight gain (S045) or low weight (S044), but it doesn't directly map to a new, unaddressed symptom profile. The patient has already provided information about both S045 (fear of weight gain/checking) and S046 (body image disturbance/shape influence). There is no distinct symptom profile left to answer this highly specific follow-up question that tries to tease apart the cognitive components.

patient.answer:
I guess I'm not really sure how to separate those, either. I mean, they all kind of blend together for me. 

If I eat something heavier, I feel bad because I worry it'll change my shape, and I worry it'll make the number on the scale go up. It's just... all of it. I haven't really noticed if one bothers me more than the other. They just all make me feel like I've messed up.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's fear of weight gain is primarily tied to concerns about body shape/appearance versus concerns about self-control or discipline, which will help distinguish between Anorexia Nervosa (F50.0) and Atypical Anorexia Nervosa (F50.1).
doctor.question: When you think about gaining weight, is your main concern about how it would change the way you look, or is it more about what it would mean for your sense of control or discipline?

target_item.reason: The doctor is repeatedly asking the same question about the underlying motivation for fearing weight gain (appearance vs. control), which the patient has already addressed multiple times using the Fear_of_Weight_Gain symptom. Since the patient has already answered this specific nuance and expressed inability to separate the two concepts, there is no new symptom profile item to provide.

patient.answer:
I... I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, Doctor. It's just like I was saying a minute ago. I really can't separate them. 

Changing the way I look and losing my discipline... to me, they are the exact same thing. If my body changes, it means I didn't have discipline. I just don't have a way to pick one over the other for you. They're completely tied together.
